title: 1970 Greater London Council election
summary: The Conservatives, under Desmond Plummer, held the Greater London Council with a reduced majority, taking 65 of the 100 seats. Labour recovered ground lost in 1967, mainly in working-class areas, regaining several boroughs. Turnout was low at 35.2%.
highlights: Conservatives hold the GLC with 65 of 100 seats
Labour recovers to 35 seats after its 1967 collapse
Labour's gains helped persuade Harold Wilson to call an early general election

council.note: 100 councillors elected from borough-based multi-member electoral areas, plus 16 aldermen chosen by the council.
